question: You file as head of household and a child is your qualifying child for the earned income credit. Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household? Under Married Filing Jointly in the 2025 Form 1040 instructions, you are married for this question if you were married at the end of 2025, even if you did not live with your spouse at the end of 2025, or if your spouse died in 2025 and you did not remarry in 2025, or if you were married at the end of 2025 and your spouse died in 2026 before filing a 2025 return. Under Single in those instructions, you are not married for this question if you were never married, or if you were widowed before January 1, 2025, and did not remarry before the end of 2025. Under Head of Household in those instructions, an interlocutory decree still means you are married, and a final decree of divorce or of separate maintenance at the end of 2025 means you are considered unmarried. A spouse who died is not a decree of separate maintenance. You remain married for this question if you are married and your spouse was a nonresident alien at any time during the year and the election to treat that spouse as a resident was not made. Publication 596, Rule 3, still treats you as married when you file as head of household under the special rules for married taxpayers living apart, including when you lived apart and are considered unmarried for head of household. Answer yes if you were married at the end of 2025, if your spouse died in 2025 and you did not remarry in 2025, if your spouse died in 2026 before filing a 2025 return, if an interlocutory decree means you are married, if your spouse was a nonresident alien and the resident election was not made, or if Rule 3 still treats you as married. Yes continues to the separated-spouse questions. Answer no if you were never married, if you were widowed before January 1, 2025, and did not remarry before the end of 2025, or if a final decree of divorce or of separate maintenance at the end of 2025 means you are considered unmarried. No skips questions 4 and 5 and continues to question 6.
